description: Guide a student to find and fix a look-ahead bias in an SMA crossover strategy where positions use today's signal without shifting, causing the strategy to 'see' future prices.

student_openings.beginner_no_finance: I built an SMA crossover strategy and it performs amazingly well! But my friend says the results are 'too good to be true.' The strategy uses 10 and 30-day moving averages. Can you help me check if something is wrong?
student_openings.intermediate_developer: I've implemented an SMA(10)/SMA(30) crossover backtest and the returns look suspiciously high. I suspect there might be a look-ahead bias but I'm not sure where. Can you help me audit the code?
student_openings.advanced_quant: My SMA crossover strategy shows inflated alpha that disappears in live trading. I suspect a temporal alignment issue in how positions are assigned relative to signal generation. Can you review my backtest code?

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Student identifies the look-ahead bias (Position = Signal without shift(1)), understands why using today's signal for today's trade is invalid, and fixes by shifting the position by 1 day.
required_capabilities: Read and understand the signal generation code
Identify the temporal alignment issue (no shift on position)
Explain why this constitutes look-ahead bias
Fix the bug by adding shift(1) to the position assignment
Verify that returns decrease after the fix (expected behavior)
